guards.what: N1: the damage amount is `base.Owner.PlayerCombatState.TurnNumber` (MrStruggles.cs:21) vs `self.turn` == CombatState.turn (mr_struggles.py:28)
guards.rationale: The two counters agree, including on the case that could have broken them. PlayerCombatState.TurnNumber starts at 1 (PlayerCombatState.cs:37) and is incremented by IncrementTurnNumber (cs:157-159) from CombatManager's side switch (CombatManager.cs:1405-1418); crucially that code increments TurnNumber for an EXTRA player turn while leaving `_state.RoundNumber` alone, and the source's own doc comment (PlayerCombatState.cs:33-36) names Pael's Eye as the reason. The sim's CombatState.turn also starts at 1 (combat.py) and increments on BOTH the ordinary boundary (combat.py) and the extra-turn path (combat.py), so it tracks TurnNumber and not RoundNumber -- the right one for this relic. The sim has a single counter serving both C# concepts; nothing in this relic reads RoundNumber, so the conflation is not observable here. Rule 7: leans on combat.py and the two C# files, none hashed here.

guards.rationale: DamageProps.NON_CARD_UNPOWERED (valueprops.py:42) is `ValueProp.UNPOWERED` alone, matching exactly: the damage is NOT boosted by Strength (is_powered_attack requires MOVE, valueprops.py:47-49), IS blockable (no Unblockable flag), and is not a 'hit' for on_attacked/Curl Up (cmds.py:69 gates that on MOVE). Note this relic has NO CanonicalVars/DamageVar at all -- the amount is the live turn number, so there is no constant to check and no AscensionHelper branch anywhere in the file. The port passes `dealer=self.combat.player`, which is the same creature as the hook's `player` argument that relic/mercury_hourglass passes.

The owner check is single-player-structural -- on_player_turn_started only fires for the player. On the enemy set: C# passes `combatState.HittableEnemies` == `Enemies.Where(e => e.IsHittable)` (CombatState.cs:142), and IsHittable is `!IsDead && Hook.ShouldAllowHitting(CombatState, this)` (Creature.cs:285-299). The sim passes Relic.living_enemies() (relics/base.py), which filters only `not e.is_gone` (dead or escaped) -- but the missing predicate IS applied, one target later, by DamageCmd.deal itself: `if not hooks.should_allow_hitting(target): return 0` (cmds.py:51-52). So for a DAMAGE call site the two sets are observationally identical (an alive-but-unhittable enemy is iterated and then takes 0). DELIBERATELY DISTINGUISHED from relic/bag_of_marbles guard G2, which records the same call-site substitution as a gap: that site routes through PowerCmd.apply, which has NO such backstop (audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json gap G6, the missing CanReceivePowers check). Same substitution, different downstream, so different verdicts -- and binding rule 3 is satisfied because the MECHANISM under verdict there is the missing PowerCmd backstop, not living_enemies() itself. The `escaped` half is also covered: an escaped creature is IsDead-or-removed in C# and is_gone in the sim.
